title: Revealing nuclear receptor hub modules from Basal-like breast cancer expression networks.
authors: Hsu, Sharon Nienyun; Hui, Erika Wong En; Liu, Mengzhen; Wu, Di; Hughes, Thomas A; Smith, James
one_liner_zh: 该研究用无监督聚类和基因相关网络分析乳腺癌中核受体转录调控模块，虽涉及转录因子但无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅网络统计，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: Nuclear receptors are a class of transcriptional factors. Together with their co-regulators, they regulate development, homeostasis, and metabolism in a ligand-dependent manner. Their ability to respond to environmental stimuli rapidly makes them versatile cellular components. Their coordinated activities regulate essential pathways in normal physiology and in disease. Due to their complexity, the challenge remains in understanding their direct associations in cancer development. Basal-like breast cancer is an aggressive form of breast cancer that often lacks ER, PR and Her2. The absence of these receptors limits the treatment for patients to the non-selective cytotoxic and cytostatic drugs. To identify potential drug targets it is essential to identify the most important nuclear receptor association network motifs in Basal-like subtype progression. This research aimed to reveal the transcriptional network patterns, in the hope to capture the underlying molecular state driving Basal-like oncogenesis. In this work, we illustrate a multidisciplinary approach of integrating an unsupervised machine learning clustering method with network modelling to reveal unique transcriptional patterns (network motifs) underlying Basal-like breast cancer. The unsupervised clustering method provides a natural stratification of breast cancer patients, revealing the underlying heterogeneity in Basal-like. Identification of gene correlation networks (GCNs) from Basal-like patients in both the TCGA and METABRIC databases revealed three critical transcriptional regulatory constellations that are enriched in Basal-like. These represent critical NR components implicated in Basal-like breast cancer transcription. This approach is easily adaptable and applicable to reveal critical signalling relationships in other diseases.
abstract_zh: 核受体是一类转录因子。它们与其共调节因子一起，以配体依赖性方式调节发育、稳态和代谢。它们对环境刺激快速响应的能力使其成为多功能的细胞组分。它们的协调活动调节正常生理和疾病中的关键通路。由于其复杂性，理解它们在癌症发展中的直接关联仍是一个挑战。基底样乳腺癌是一种侵袭性乳腺癌形式，通常缺乏ER、PR和Her2。这些受体的缺失限制了患者的治疗选择，只能使用非选择性细胞毒性和细胞抑制药物。为了识别潜在的药物靶点，必须确定基底样亚型进展中最重要的核受体关联网络基序。本研究旨在揭示转录网络模式，以期捕捉驱动基底样肿瘤发生的潜在分子状态。在这项工作中，我们展示了一种多学科方法，将无监督机器学习聚类方法与网络建模相结合，以揭示基底样乳腺癌背后的独特转录模式（网络基序）。无监督聚类方法提供了乳腺癌患者的自然分层，揭示了基底样中的潜在异质性。在TCGA和METABRIC数据库中，从基底样患者中识别基因相关网络（GCNs）揭示了三个在基底样中富集的关键转录调控星座。这些代表了与基底样乳腺癌转录相关的关键核受体组分。该方法易于调整和适用，可用于揭示其他疾病中的关键信号关系。
